paper.title: Metabolomic machine learning predictor for diagnosis and prognosis of gastric cancer

claims.text: Targeted plasma metabolomics of 702 participants (389 GC, 313 NGC) reveals a reprogrammed metabolic landscape in GC, with 45 differential metabolites and disturbed glutathione/cysteine-methionine pathways.
A 10-metabolite diagnostic model (10-DM, LASSO + random forest) discriminates GC from NGC in test set 1 with AUROC 0.967 (95% CI 0.944-0.987), sensitivity 0.854, specificity 0.926.
The 10-DM model validates in an external test set (Cohort 2, n=95) with AUROC 0.920, sensitivity 0.905, specificity 0.75.
The 10-DM model detects early-stage GC (stage IA/IB in test set 1; stage IA and stage I+II in test set 2) with high sensitivity.
The 10-DM model outperforms the conventional 3-biomarker panel (CA19-9, CA72-4, CEA) and other machine-learning algorithms (SVM, LR, RF, PLS-DA in MetaboAnalyst).
claims.location: Abstract; Results 'Comparison of the diagnostic performance'; Supplementary Fig. 4

claims.text: A 28-metabolite random-survival-forest prognostic model (28-PM) predicts GC outcome in the test set with c-index 0.83 and AUROC 0.832 (95% CI 0.697-0.951).

The 28-PM model outperforms clinical parameters (TNM staging, macroscopic appearance, vascular tumor embolus) individually and combined, and adding clinical parameters improves performance by only ~1%.
claims.location: Results 'The addition of clinical parameters...'; Fig. 4d; Supplementary Fig. 5c

claims.text: Risk stratification by the 28-PM cutoff (2.1) separates high- and low-risk patients with different OS/DFS and different deceased/relapse proportions.
The 28-PM metabolic risk group is an independent prognostic factor in multivariate Cox regression (HR 7.53, 95% CI 2.83-20.04, P=5.276e-5).

findings.evidence: The paper reports "95% confidence" intervals, but the code computes the interval with 5%/95% bounds (`confidence_lower = sorted_scores[int(0.05 * len(sorted_scores))]`) (and 1 similar line(s)), which is a 90% interval; no 2.5%/97.5% bounds appear anywhere in the code. Check whether the reported intervals are 90% intervals.
findings.question_for_authors: Are the reported confidence intervals 95% or 90% intervals?
